title: Dev releases run nightly at 02:00 UTC; a staging line that is not one semver step from main needs a hand-set baseline one prerelease below the intended first publish
content:
**Dev.** `main` auto-releases every night at 02:00 UTC via the workflow's cron. An immediate dev release is Release Branch on `main` with `release_mode=prerelease`, publishing `X.Y.Z-dev.N+1`.

**Staging** has three cases:

- **Case 1 — fresh line, target one semver step from main.** Branch `release/staging/<X.Y.Z>` off `main`, push, run the workflow: `prerelease` → `X.Y.Z-staging.1`, `patch` → `X.Y.(Z+1)-staging.1`, `minor` / `major` likewise.
- **Case 2 — next prerelease on an existing staging branch.** Merge `origin/main` into it. `package.json` (root and every workspace) and `CHANGELOG.md` almost always conflict; **always keep the staging side** of the `"version"` fields and changelog content, or the next release bumps from `-dev.N` and ships the wrong tag. Fast path: `git checkout --ours -- package.json '**/package.json' CHANGELOG.md '**/CHANGELOG.md'`, then `prerelease`.
- **Case 3 — fresh line at a non-adjacent version** (e.g. main at `6.0.0-dev.239`, target `6.0.3-staging.1` because 6.0.1 and 6.0.2 were already cut). Semver `inc()` only steps by one, and the workflow has no "publish exactly this version" mode, so set the baseline by hand **one prerelease number below** the desired first publish: `npx nx release version 6.0.3-staging.0`, sanity-check with `git grep -h '"version":' -- '**/package.json' | sort -u`, commit `chore(release): set baseline …`, push, then run `prerelease` — Nx bumps `.0 → .1`. This is the one case where a human edits versions. If the run fails after the baseline commit, just retrigger: the baseline is still on the branch.

Staging releases require no release notes or Discord post; those belong to the production flow, whose branch is `release/production/<label>` and which always uses `patch`, `minor` or `major`.
